name: Tr’ondëk-Klondike
description: Tr'ondëk-Klondike lies along the Yukon River in northwestern Canada, around Dawson City, in the homeland of the Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in First Nation. Its name comes from the Hän word for "hammerstone water." The sites trace how this Indigenous community adapted when the 1896–99 Klondike Gold Rush brought a flood of newcomers, from places of exchange with colonists to settlements shaped by their arrival.
